item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 220511
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 AM EDT Thu Oct 22 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Subtropical
Storm Josephine, located a few hundred miles offshore of the
Mid-Atlantic coast of the United States.

Subtropical Central Atlantic:
A trough of low pressure located several hundred miles to the
east-southeast of Bermuda is producing a large area of disorganized
showers and thunderstorms. Some development of this system is
possible during the next day or two while it moves slowly
north-northeastward. Upper-level winds are forecast to become too
strong for further development by the weekend.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...10 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Josephine are issued under WMO header WTNT35
KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPAT5.
Forecast/Advisories on Josephine are issued under WMO header WTNT25
KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMAT5.

$$
Forecaster Gibbs

item.title: Subtropical Storm Josephine Public Advisory Number 3
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM AST Thu Oct 22 2026 
000
WTNT35 KNHC 220847
TCPAT5
 
BULLETIN
Subtropical Storm Josephine Advisory Number   3
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL102026
500 AM AST Thu Oct 22 2026
 
...JOSEPHINE ACCELERATING NORTHEASTWARD AWAY FROM THE UNITED
STATES...
...EXPECTED TO BECOME A POWERFUL EXTRATROPICAL CYCLONE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 AM AST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...38.7N 68.3W
ABOUT 195 MI...315 KM SSE OF NANTUCKET MASSACHUSETTS
ABOUT 475 MI...765 KM SSW OF HALIFAX NOVA SCOTIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NE OR 40 DEGREES AT 13 MPH...20 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...988 MB...29.18 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM AST (0900 UTC), the center of Subtropical Storm Josephine
was located near latitude 38.7 North, longitude 68.3 West. The storm 
is moving toward the northeast near 13 mph (20 km/h), and this 
motion, along with an increase in forward speed, is expected to 
continue into tonight. A gradual turn toward the east is forecast on 
Friday and into the weekend. On the forecast track, Josephine should 
move away from the United States and remain south of Nova Scotia and 
Newfoundland during the next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Some additional strengthening is forecast through the day 
today while Josephine begins to transition to an extratropical 
cyclone. Josephine is expected to become a powerful extratropical 
cyclone with hurricane-force winds by early Friday.
 
Winds of 40 mph extend outward up to 415 miles (665 km) from the
center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 988 mb (29.18 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
WIND: Gale-force winds are possible in gusts along portions of the
northeastern United States coast through today. See products issued
by your local National Weather Service office for more details.
 
COASTAL FLOODING: Minor to locally moderate coastal flooding is
ongoing along portions of the U.S. Mid-Atlantic coast and will
continue through the rest of the week around times of high tide.
Please refer to products issued by your local National Weather
Service forecast office for more information.
 
SURF: Large swells generated by Josephine are affecting much of the
eastern seaboard of the United States and portions of Atlantic
Canada. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and
rip current conditions. Please consult products from your local
weather office.
 
A depiction of rip current risk for the United States can be found
at: hurricanes.gov/graphics_at5.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 AM AST.
 
$$
Forecaster Gibbs
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Subtropical Storm Josephine Forecast Discussion Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM AST Wed Oct 21 2026 
000
WTNT45 KNHC 220256
TCDAT5
 
Subtropical Storm Josephine Discussion Number   2
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL102026
1100 PM AST Wed Oct 21 2026
 
Convection associated with Josephine has waned this evening. The 
latest satellite images show shallow to moderate convection in bands 
over the northern and western portions of the circulation. Despite 
its degraded satellite structure, partial scatterometer data show 
Josephine is still a powerful storm with a large radius of maximum 
wind and an asymmetric wind field. A band of 45-50 kt winds wraps 
around the northwest side of the system. Since the entire wind field 
was not sampled, the initial intensity is held at a possibly 
generous 55 kt for this advisory.
 
Recent satellite fixes indicate Josephine is now moving slowly
north-northeastward (015/5 kt). The storm is expected to accelerate
to the northeast and east-northeast tomorrow as an upper-level
trough amplifies over the Canadian Maritimes and the northeastern
United States. Then, the low should become caught in mid-latitude
westerlies and move eastward on Friday and into the weekend, with
the center passing to the south of Newfoundland late Friday and
Friday night. The track model guidance remains tightly clustered,
and the NHC forecast is very similar to the previous one, generally
falling between the corrected consensus (HCCA) and a simple average
of the GFS/ECMWF models (GFEX).
 
Josephine is unlikely to remain subtropical for long since the storm
will encounter much cooler waters and stronger shear over the next
12-24 hours. However, the global models favor some near-term
strengthening driven mostly by baroclinic processes and positive
interaction with the approaching trough. This forecast shows
Josephine becoming a hurricane-force, extratropical cyclone in 24 h,
though it could lose subtropical characteristics even sooner.
Gradual weakening is predicted beginning on Friday, and the updated
forecast shows Josephine becoming absorbed by 96 h within a larger,
extratropical low over the North Atlantic. Given the subtropical
nature of this storm, the NHC intensity forecast continues to favor
a blend of the GFS and ECMWF models.
 
Since the coastal wind hazards with this system have been covered
for the last several days through non-tropical products issued by
local National Weather Service offices, these products will remain
in effect until the threat diminishes and the system moves farther
away from the U.S. coast.
